# Dependencies & Preparation

First we import the required libraries and set up the paths.
We also assume that the `coderdata` package is installed and available in the Python environment. 

We can then download the latest version of the coderdata dataset, using the following command in the terminal:

```{bash}
#| label: download data
#| warning: FALSE
#| eval: FALSE
coderdata download --local_path '/tmp'
```

We can now set up `reticulate` to interface with Python from R.


```{r}
#| label: imports-and-setup
#| warning: FALSE

# r libraries
library(reticulate)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(patchwork)
library(GSVA) ##do to the enrichment statistics

# path setupd
data_dir <- "/tmp/"

#wd <- tempdir()
#setwd(wd)
reticulate::use_virtualenv('r-reticulate')
reticulate::import("coderdata")

# defines the python environment to use
py_require("coderdata")

# import the coderdata package from python
cd <- import("coderdata")


```

Once we have loaded the `coderdata` package, we can check the version and list the 
available datasets to confirm that we have the correct version and datasets available.
```{r}
#| label: confirm-version-and-datasets
cd$version()
cd$list_datasets()
```

# Drug data import
Now we are ready to load the datasets and format them for analysis. We will load the
 cell line datasets to load the relevant experimental,
drug, proteomic, and transcriptomic data for each dataset.

Note how this is done using the `reticulate` functionality to call Python functions from R via `cd$load(...)` and `datasets[[name]]$format(...)`.

```{r}
#| label: load-datasets
#| warning: FALSE
#| echo: FALSE


datasetnames <- c("ccle", "ctrpv2", "prism", "gdscv1", "gdscv2", "nci60")
datasets <- list()

for (name in datasetnames) {
  datasets[[name]] <- cd$load(name, local_path = data_dir)
}

experiments <- list()
transcripts <- list()
proteomics <- list()

for (name in datasetnames) {
  experiments[[name]] <- datasets[[name]]$format(
    "experiments",
    shape = "wide",
    metrics = "fit_auc")

    transcripts[[name]] <- datasets[[name]]$format(
    "transcriptomics",
    shape = "matrix",
    metrics = "transcripomics"
  )
    proteomics[[name]] <- datasets[[name]]$format(
    "proteomics",
    shape = "matrix",
    metrics = "proteomics"
  )
}
```


Now we have the transcripts data, each as a matrix. We can take a set of genes and identify 
specific drugs that are correlated with samples that are active in those.

## RNA-based correlations with drug response

We can try to do two-sided test to ask if there is enrichment on both ends, and then
just reverse the sign for each condition.

```{r}
#| label: collect test results fo gene
#| warning: false

##load in coderdata file. remember we're working in a random directory because of reticulate issues. 
source("../scripts/coderdata_drug_rank.R")
convert_genes <- function(genelist, genemapping){
  res <- genemapping |> 
    subset(gene_symbol %in%genelist)
  return(unique(res$entrez_id))
}

rna.results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(datasetnames, function(ds){
  print(paste('ranking',ds))
  rank_coderdata_drugs(
     omics_matrix = t(transcripts[[ds]]),
     experiment_data = experiments[[ds]],
     signatures = list(chr8 = convert_genes(RNA.genelist.chr8, datasets[[ds]]$genes),
                        wt = convert_genes(RNA.genelist.wt, datasets[[ds]]$genes)),
     #drug_data = datasets[[ds]]$drugs,
     adjust_scope = 'global',
     modality = "transcriptomics",
     method = "ssgsea",
     association = "spearman"
  )$ranking |> 
    mutate(dataset = ds)
}))

top_rna <- subset(rna.results, fdr<0.05) |>
  subset(association <0) |>
  group_by(improve_drug_id, signature)|> 
  summarize(ndatasets= n_distinct(dataset)) 


subset(rna.results, fdr<0.05) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x=association, fill = dataset)) + geom_density() + facet_grid(signature~.)

```

Now we have the transcriptomics results we can now look at the proteomics results.

## Proteomics based drug correlations

We can run the same code on the proteomics data

```{r}
#| label: proteomics lists
#| warning: false
#| 
prot.results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(datasetnames, function(ds){
  rank_coderdata_drugs(
     omics_matrix = t(proteomics[[ds]]),
     experiment_data = experiments[[ds]],
     signatures = list(chr8 = convert_genes(prot.genelist.chr8, datasets[[ds]]$genes),
                        wt = convert_genes(prot.genelist.wt, datasets[[ds]]$genes)),
     #drug_data = datasets[[ds]]$drugs,
     modality = "proteomics",
     method = "ssgsea",
     adjust_scope = 'global',
     association = "spearman"
  )$ranking |> 
    mutate(dataset = ds)
}))

top_prot <- subset(prot.results, fdr<0.05) |>
  subset(association <0) |>
  group_by(improve_drug_id, signature)|> 
  summarize(ndatasets= n_distinct(dataset)) 

subset(prot.results, fdr<0.05) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x=association, fill = dataset)) + 
  geom_density() + 
  facet_grid(signature~.) + 
  ggtitle("Correlations with protein scores, negative implies increase drug sensitivity")

```

Now we can use a second script I added to create a mapping of common drug names.
```{bash}

python ../scripts/create_common_drug_names.py --data-dir='/tmp/'

```
Now we can combine the two and add in the new drug annotation file that we might keep. 

```{r combined results}

drug_names <-readr::read_csv('common_drug_names.csv')

combined.res <- rbind(prot.results, rna.results) |>
  left_join(drug_names)

combined.res |>
  subset(fdr<0.05) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x=association, fill = dataset)) + geom_density() + facet_grid(signature~modality) +
  ggtitle("Significant associations with drug response across signatures and omes")


drug.counts <- combined.res |> 
    subset(fdr<0.05) |> 
    subset(association <0) |>
    group_by(signature, improve_drug_id) |> 
    summarize(ndat = n_distinct(dataset), num_modes = n_distinct(modality)) |> 
    subset(ndat>1 | num_modes>1) |>
    arrange(desc(ndat))

###list the drugs with an average rank below 10?
ranks <- combined.res |>
    group_by(signature, common_name, modality) |> 
    summarize(mrank = median(rank), ndataset = n_distinct(dataset)) |>
    arrange(mrank)

subset(ranks, ndataset>2) |>
  subset(mrank < 150) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x=common_name, y=mrank, size = ndataset, shape = signature, col=modality))+
  geom_point() + 
  coord_flip() + 
  ggtitle('Top drugs for Chr8 amplified vs WT MPNST')

```

# Empircal testing
We can evaluate a test dataset based on a specific cell line? 

Quick test:
1. take a drug of interest
2. rank cell lines by the AUC
For each cell line:
  3. those that are the most negative - get genes that overlap?
  4. can we get those genes and find drug again? 




The challenge we have is trying to figure out which
